# SSO + 3 roles

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:console-sso-rbac` · **Epic:** [#30](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/30) · **Tickets:** 8 (4S 4M)

The control-plane console gets its first authentication. Today `/dashboard/*` is mounted with no auth at all (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go `mux.Handle("/dashboard/", dash.Handler())`), including the routes that write real secret values. With `console.auth: oidc`, humans sign in to Dex (or any OIDC issuer) with auth code + PKCE, get a server-side session, and are mapped from IdP groups to admin, editor or viewer. Every dashboard route is checked against a method-and-path role table that denies anything not listed, and the shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN is never accepted on human routes. `console.auth: none` stays the default and keeps today's open console, with warnings.

## How we build it

- Scope: CP only. Worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /healthz) keep their current bearer check and are not touched. The worker-local dashboard mount (internal/worker/worker.go:581 `adminMux.Handle("/dashboard/", dashSrv.Handler())`) keeps its current behaviour; authz wraps only the CP mount.
- New package `internal/cpstate`: one SQLite DB `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` (modernc.org/sqlite, already in go.mod), single connection with WAL and busy_timeout like internal/integration/store.go, and a forward-only `schema_migrations(id, applied_at)` table keyed by string IDs such as `sessions/0001` so features never collide. A DB that holds an unknown migration ID or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup (fail-closed). OIDC console mode requires `--state-dir`.
- CP-local `console:` block (`json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire): `auth: none|oidc`, `oidc: {issuer, clientID (default warden-console), clientSecretEnv, redirectURL, scopes, allowInsecureIssuer}`, `roles: {admin, editor, viewer: [groups]}`, `session: {idle: 1h, absolute: 12h}` (fixed defaults). The CP reads it only from the operator-owned `--config` file, never from the `<state-dir>/config.yaml` copy, which is seeded once (seedServedConfig in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go) and rewritten by the dashboard writers. A differing console block in the served copy is ignored with a warning.
- Login: `GET /auth/login` stores state, nonce, an S256 PKCE verifier and the `next` path in a cpstate `oidc_pending` row (10 min TTL, single use, capped) bound to the browser by a short-lived login cookie. `GET /auth/callback` consumes the row atomically, exchanges the code with golang.org/x/oauth2 (new dependency), and verifies the ID token with a new `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier`, a thin wrapper over the W-P1-VRFY-01 OIDC verifier, that checks aud contains clientID, azp equals clientID when present or when aud has several entries, the nonce, RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew. The console uses its own Dex client `warden-console`, separate from the `warden` agent-token client. The identity key is (iss, sub); email is for display only.
- Degraded modes: OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff, so a Dex outage never stops the CP from starting or serving workers. While the IdP is unreachable only /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`; existing sessions keep working. Session expiry uses the CP clock only, and sessions survive CP restarts. The IdP-down admin path is break-glass (p1-breakglass).
- Sessions: a fresh 32-byte random id on every login, stored only as sha256 in `sessions`. Cookie `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https; plain `warden_console` only for an http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer setup, with a warning. Secure follows the redirectURL scheme, not the local listener, so a TLS-terminating ingress works. The CSRF token is an HMAC of the raw session id, sent in `X-Warden-CSRF` on every non-GET request together with an Origin check against the redirectURL origin.
- Roles: the session stores the IdP groups, and the role is recomputed on every request from the current `console.roles` (admin > editor > viewer). A login whose groups match no role creates no session. Admins can list and revoke sessions. IdP group changes take effect at the next login, so the 12h absolute lifetime bounds offboarding lag unless an admin revokes earlier.
- Authz: `dashboard.Routes()` exports every {method, path, action} the dashboard registers. A CP middleware applies a table keyed by {method, path} giving the minimum role and an action name (reused by p1-admin-audit). Viewer: every GET, plus POST query and audit/verify. Editor: POST query/generate (it spends LLM tokens; also limited to 10 per minute per session), POST/PUT policy and detection, and settings writes that touch only editor fields. Admin: POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore, /central/secrets and sessions. A {method, path} not in the table is denied, and a coverage test fails on any route missing from it.
- Settings writes are authorized per field. Editor may change only advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents and cacheTTLSeconds. Any other difference from the live SettingsWire (llmProviders, secrets, explore, judge, observability, mcp, and fields added later such as identity) needs admin, because those can change where workers send real credentials. A denial returns 403 with the field names.
- The request Principal is `{Kind: session|breakglass|apikey, Iss, Sub, Email, Groups, AuthMethod}`, so p1-breakglass, p1-admin-audit and p2 API keys reuse the same table. In oidc mode WARDEN_CP_TOKEN opens no /dashboard/* or /central/secrets route; it stays valid on worker routes until p1-worker-tokens.
- Back-compat: a missing `console` block means `auth: none`; the console stays open as today and compose recipes keep working. none mode logs a startup warning, `/dashboard/api/setup` returns `authMode`, the UI shows a banner, and a new `--require-console-auth` flag refuses to start in none mode. Logs carry `console_login`, `console_logout`, `console_authz_denied` and `console_session_revoked` records, never tokens, codes, cookies or secret values.

## Done when

On a CP started with `console.auth: oidc` in --config, an https redirectURL and an existing --state-dir: an unauthenticated request, or one carrying only the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN bearer, gets 401 on every /dashboard/api/* route and on /central/secrets, while workers keep pulling /policy. An LDAP user in warden-viewers can read every tab but gets 403 on POST /dashboard/api/policy and POST /dashboard/api/secretstore. A warden-editors user can edit policy and toggle DLP but gets 403 when a settings change touches llmProviders or the secrets backend. Only warden-admins can edit integrations, LLM providers and secrets, and can revoke a live session, which then gets 401. A POST without a matching X-Warden-CSRF header gets 403, the CP still starts and serves workers with Dex stopped, and a route-coverage test fails if any dashboard route has no authz entry.

### 1/8 · W-P1-SSO-01

**Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#31](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/31)

Create new package `internal/cpstate` that opens one SQLite DB at `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` and runs forward-only migrations registered by each feature store. This ticket ships only the runner and test migrations: `oidc_pending` comes in W-P1-SSO-03 and `sessions` in W-P1-SSO-04. It follows the single-connection modernc pattern already used in internal/integration/store.go and internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go, so it is small. Admin audit, policy versions, worker tokens and backups build on this file.

**Requirements**

- API: `Open(ctx, path string, migs []Migration) (*DB, error)`, `(*DB).Close() error`, `(*DB).SQL() *sql.DB`, with `Migration{ID string; SQL string}`. `OpenReadOnly(ctx, path)` opens the file with `mode=ro`, applies no migrations, still runs quick_check and the unknown-ID check, and is what offline readers such as W-P1-AAUD-04 use. IDs are unique strings such as `sessions/0001`, so migrations from different features never collide.
- `schema_migrations(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)`. Each migration and its row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls back both.
- Downgrade guard: if the DB holds a migration ID the binary does not register, Open returns an error naming that ID and leaves the file unchanged.
- Connection settings match the repo: `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` and DSN pragmas journal_mode(WAL), busy_timeout(5000), foreign_keys(1). The file is created with mode 0600.
- Fail-closed: a file that is not a database or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup with an error naming the path and a hint to restore from backup or move the file aside.
- cmd/proxy opens the DB only when `--state-dir` is set and passes it in a new `controlplane.Config.State *cpstate.DB` field; without `--state-dir` State is nil and CP behaviour is unchanged. The DB is closed after the HTTP server drains.
- One startup log line with fields `db` and `applied` (migration IDs). Row contents are never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/cpstate/cpstate.go (new) with DB, Migration and Open, using sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)") and SetMaxOpenConns(1) as in internal/integration/store.go; chmod the file to 0600 after create.
2. In Open, run `PRAGMA quick_check` and return a wrapped error when it does not return `ok`.
3. Create internal/cpstate/migrate.go (new): create schema_migrations, read applied IDs, refuse unknown IDs, then apply each missing Migration in the order passed, one transaction each.
4. In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go runControlPlane, when stateDir != "", call cpstate.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(stateDir, "warden-cp.db"), nil) and set the new controlplane.Config.State field (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go); close it after shutdown.
5. Add internal/cpstate/cpstate_test.go (new) with two migration sets, an unknown-ID DB, a failing migration, a garbage file and 50 concurrent writers.
6. Extend cmd/proxy/commands_test.go: TestControlPlaneSubcommand_StateDir asserts warden-cp.db exists with mode 0600, and a new TestControlPlaneCorruptStateDB covers the fail-closed exit.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a DB with migration `t/0001`, when Open runs with {`t/0001`, `t/0002`}, then only `t/0002` is applied: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestMigrateAppliesOnlyNew`
- [ ] Given a DB that holds `t/0003`, when a binary registering only `t/0001` and `t/0002` opens it, then Open fails naming `t/0003` and the file bytes are unchanged: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestMigrateRefusesUnknownID`
- [ ] Given a migration whose SQL fails, when Open runs, then its ID is not recorded and earlier tables are intact
- [ ] Given 50 goroutines doing 100 inserts each, when run with -race, then none returns SQLITE_BUSY: `go test -race ./internal/cpstate -run TestConcurrentWriters`
- [ ] Given a warden-cp.db of random bytes, when the control plane starts, then it exits non-zero with an error naming the path: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneCorruptStateDB`
- [ ] Without --state-dir, existing CP tests pass unchanged: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane`
- [ ] Given an existing DB, when OpenReadOnly is used and a write is attempted, then the write fails and the file's bytes and mtime are unchanged: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestOpenReadOnly`

### 2/8 · W-P1-SSO-02

**Parse and validate the CP-local console config block**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#32](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/32)

Add the CP-local `console:` config block with strict parsing, validation and a pure `RoleFor(groups)` function used at login. The CP reads it only from the operator-owned `--config` file, because the `--state-dir` copy is seeded once and rewritten by the dashboard, so edits there would be ignored or could be changed from the UI. Break-glass fields are left to W-P1-OPS1-01. Until W-P1-SSO-05 lands, cmd/proxy refuses to start with `console.auth: oidc`, so no build ever runs with login routes but no enforcement.

**Requirements**

- internal/config/console.go (new): `ConsoleConfig{Auth string; OIDC ConsoleOIDC; Roles ConsoleRoles; Session ConsoleSession}`, `ConsoleOIDC{Issuer, ClientID, ClientSecretEnv, RedirectURL string; Scopes []string; AllowInsecureIssuer bool}`, `ConsoleRoles{Admin, Editor, Viewer []string}`, `ConsoleSession{Idle, Absolute time.Duration}`, and `type Role int` with RoleViewer < RoleEditor < RoleAdmin.
- Defaults: an absent block means Auth=none; clientID defaults to `warden-console`, the reference console client from W-P1-DEX-01; Scopes default to [openid, email, profile, groups]; Idle 1h; Absolute 12h (the decided defaults; not 8h/24h). Any Auth value other than none or oidc is a validation error.
- oidc validation: issuer, clientSecretEnv and redirectURL are required and clientID must be non-empty after defaulting; issuer and redirectURL must be https unless the host is loopback or allowInsecureIssuer is true; redirectURL must be absolute and end in /auth/callback; at least one admin group; 0 < Idle <= Absolute <= 168h.
- `Policy.Console ConsoleConfig` has `json:"-"`, so it never appears on policyWire or SettingsWire. rawConfig accepts the `console:` key under KnownFields(true), so workers and the served copy still parse.
- New `config.LoadConsole(path string) (ConsoleConfig, error)`. cmd/proxy calls it on `--config`, not the served path; if the served copy holds a different console block it logs a warning and ignores it. Changing the block needs a CP restart.
- `func (c ConsoleConfig) RoleFor(groups []string) (Role, bool)` is pure; the highest matching role wins.
- At startup in oidc mode: an empty `os.Getenv(clientSecretEnv)` or a missing `--state-dir` is a fatal error, logs name the env var but never its value, allowInsecureIssuer logs a warning, and a temporary guard refuses oidc with "console oidc enforcement is not available in this build" (removed by W-P1-SSO-05).

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/config/console.go (new) with the types, defaults, Role, RoleFor and validateConsole.
2. In internal/config/config.go add an unexported rawConsole and `Console *rawConsole `yaml:"console"`` to rawConfig, convert it next to the Detection assignment into Policy.Console, and call validateConsole from validate().
3. Add LoadConsole(path) in internal/config/console.go, reusing the strict decoder to read only the console node.
4. In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go add resolveConsole(opts, servedPath) (new): load from opts.configPath, compare with the served copy's block, check the secret env and --state-dir, apply the temporary oidc guard, and pass the result in a new controlplane.Config.Console field.
5. Add a commented example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml: an https production block and a compose block with issuer http://dex:5556/dex, clientID warden-console, clientSecretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirectURL https://localhost:7070/auth/callback and allowInsecureIssuer: true, matching the W-P1-DEX-01 client.
6. Tests: internal/config/console_test.go (new); internal/controlplane/console_wire_test.go (new) for policyWire (controlplane.go) and SettingsWire; writer preservation in internal/controlplane; resolveConsole cases in cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Table tests cover a valid oidc block, a missing admin group, an http non-loopback issuer without the flag (rejected), the same with allowInsecureIssuer (accepted), http://127.0.0.1 (accepted), idle > absolute (rejected), an unknown auth value (rejected) and RoleFor precedence: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestConsoleConfig|TestRoleFor'`
- [ ] Given a Policy with a fully set Console, when policyWire and SettingsWire are marshalled, then neither JSON contains `console`, `clientSecretEnv` or `roles`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestConsoleNotOnWire`
- [ ] Given a served config with a console block, when WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations and WriteDetection each persist an edit, then the console node is byte-identical: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWritersPreserveConsoleBlock`
- [ ] Given --config with console.auth=oidc and an existing --state-dir whose config.yaml has no console block, when resolveConsole runs, then it returns the --config block: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestResolveConsoleFromConfigFlag`
- [ ] Given oidc mode with an empty client secret env var, when resolveConsole runs, then it fails naming the variable and captured logs hold no secret value
- [ ] Given an existing config with no console block, when it is parsed, then Console.Auth is "none" and existing config tests pass: `go test ./internal/config`

### 3/8 · W-P1-SSO-03

**Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#33](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/33)

Add `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` on the CP mux in oidc mode, using authorization code with S256 PKCE, a browser-bound single-use pending row in cpstate, and strict ID token checks. This ticket adds a thin ID-token verifier to internal/identity on top of the W-P1-VRFY-01 OIDC verifier (Audience=clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], WithNonce), so the console shares its keyset, algorithm allowlist and skew handling. On success it maps groups to a role with `ConsoleConfig.RoleFor` and creates a session through the W-P1-SSO-04 SessionStore. It uses the `warden-console` client already defined in the reference Dex config by W-P1-DEX-01.

**Requirements**

- Routes are mounted only when console.auth=oidc and Config.State is set; in none mode they return 404. `next` is accepted only as a relative path under /dashboard/ (no scheme, no `//`, no backslash), otherwise /dashboard/ is used.
- OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff in a goroutine started from Server.Start; until it succeeds /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`, and CP startup and worker routes are unaffected.
- Migration `oidc_pending/0001`: `oidc_pending(state_hash PK, nonce, verifier, next, browser_hash, expires_at)` with a 10 min TTL. Callback consumes the row with `DELETE ... RETURNING` in one statement. Rows are swept every minute and capped at 10,000; above the cap login returns 503.
- Browser binding: /auth/login sets `__Host-warden_login` (or `warden_login` on http; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age 600) holding random bytes whose sha256 must equal browser_hash at callback; the cookie is cleared after use.
- New `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier(ctx, IDTokenConfig{Issuer, ClientID, AllowInsecureIssuer})` built on identity.NewOIDCVerifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 with Audience=ClientID, AllowedAZP=[ClientID] and WithNonce; it adds the OIDC Core rule that azp must be present and equal ClientID when aud has several entries. RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew come from the shared verifier. The callback compares the nonce in constant time.
- On success: RoleFor(groups) must match, else redirect with `login_error=no_role` and no session; groups capped at 256; SessionStore.Create issues a fresh id; offline_access is not requested and no access, refresh or ID token is stored.
- Errors redirect to `/dashboard/?login_error=<code>` with code from {state_invalid, nonce_mismatch, token_invalid, exchange_failed, idp_error, no_role, idp_unavailable}; IdP error text is never echoed.
- No Dex config change: the `warden-console` client (redirect https://localhost:7070/auth/callback, secretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET) comes from W-P1-DEX-01. Each attempt logs `msg=console_login result reason sub duration_ms`, never the code, state, verifier, nonce or tokens.

**Implementation plan**

1. Run `go get golang.org/x/oauth2@<exact version at least two weeks old>` (new; go-oidc v3 comes from W-P1-VRFY-01) and run govulncheck.
2. Add internal/identity/idtoken.go (new) with NewIDTokenVerifier wrapping identity.NewOIDCVerifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 (Claims already carries Nonce and AZP), so the JWKS cache and refetch floor are shared.
3. Create internal/controlplane/oidc_pending.go (new): migration, Put, Take(stateHash) with DELETE ... RETURNING and expiry check, Count for the cap, and Sweep(now).
4. Create internal/controlplane/auth.go (new): lazy provider with backoff, oauth2.Config{ClientID, ClientSecret, RedirectURL, Scopes, Endpoint}, handleLogin using oauth2.GenerateVerifier, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption and SetAuthURLParam("nonce"), and handleCallback using Exchange with oauth2.VerifierOption, then the ID-token verifier, RoleFor and SessionStore.Create.
5. Mount /auth/login and /auth/callback in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) only in oidc mode; start the discovery and sweeper goroutines in Server.Start.
6. Use the existing `warden-console` client and WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET from W-P1-DEX-01/02 in the docs example; do not edit deploy/compose/dex.
7. Add internal/controlplane/auth_test.go (new) with an httptest fake OIDC provider (discovery, JWKS, token endpoint, RSA key) and a fake clock, plus internal/identity/idtoken_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a fake OIDC provider, when a client follows /auth/login, the provider redirect and /auth/callback, then a sessions row exists for (iss, sub), a session cookie is set and the response redirects to `next`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCLoginEndToEnd`
- [ ] Given a replayed state, a mismatched nonce, aud=[agent-harness] only, aud=[warden-console, agent-harness] with azp=agent-harness, an expired token, or alg none/HS256, when the callback runs, then no session row is created and the redirect carries the matching login_error: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCCallbackRejects`
- [ ] Given a valid state but no matching login cookie, when the callback runs, then it fails with state_invalid
- [ ] Given next=https://evil.example or //evil.example, when login completes, then the redirect goes to /dashboard/
- [ ] Given a user whose groups match no role, when the callback runs, then no session row exists and login_error=no_role
- [ ] Given the fake provider is down at CP start, when /policy and /auth/login are requested, then /policy answers as before and /auth/login returns 503 idp_unavailable; after the provider comes up, login succeeds
- [ ] Captured logs from the end-to-end test contain none of the authorization code, verifier, nonce or raw ID token

### 4/8 · W-P1-SSO-04

**Add server-side sessions, logout, /auth/me and CSRF**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#34](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/34)

Add the `sessions` store, the session middleware that puts a Principal into the request context, the session cookie, CSRF checks, `POST /auth/logout` and `GET /auth/me`. It is built and tested by calling SessionStore.Create directly, so it lands before the login flow in W-P1-SSO-03. It also adds one `api()` fetch wrapper to the dashboard UI, because without the CSRF header every write would fail once oidc mode is enforced. This ticket authenticates but does not deny; enforcement comes in W-P1-SSO-05.

**Requirements**

- Migration `sessions/0001`: `sessions(id_hash PK, iss, sub, email, groups_json, auth_method, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at)` with indexes on expires_at and sub. `SessionStore` takes an injectable `now func() time.Time` and has Create, Lookup, Touch, Delete, DeleteBySub, List and SweepExpired.
- Every Create issues a fresh 32-byte crypto/rand id (base64url); only sha256(id) is stored. The CSRF token is HMAC-SHA256(raw id, "warden-csrf"), so it is never stored.
- Cookie: `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when console.oidc.redirectURL is https; `warden_console` without Secure only when redirectURL is http on loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning. Secure is never derived from r.TLS.
- Idle and absolute expiry use the CP clock; last_seen_at is written at most once per minute per session; expired rows are swept every minute from Server.Start.
- `Principal{Kind, Iss, Sub, Email string; Groups []string; AuthMethod string}` with WithPrincipal and PrincipalFrom(ctx). withSession is applied only to /dashboard/, /central/secrets and /auth/*, never to /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /healthz.
- CSRF: for methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS with a session, `X-Warden-CSRF` must match in constant time and Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin; otherwise 403 `{"error":"csrf"}`.
- POST /auth/logout (CSRF checked) deletes the row and clears the cookie; GET /auth/me returns `{sub,email,role,authMethod,csrf,expiresAt}` with Cache-Control: no-store, or 401. Both are mounted only in oidc mode.
- Logs show at most the first 8 hex characters of id_hash and never the cookie value or CSRF token.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/controlplane/session.go (new): the migration, SessionStore and its methods.
2. Create internal/controlplane/principal.go (new): Principal, WithPrincipal, PrincipalFrom.
3. Create internal/controlplane/session_mw.go (new): withSession (cookie read, Lookup, expiry, Touch, Principal) and the CSRF and Origin check, plus the cookie helper that picks the name and flags from RedirectURL.
4. Create internal/controlplane/auth_session.go (new): handleLogout and handleMe; mount them and wrap /dashboard/ and /central/secrets with withSession in Server.Handler only in oidc mode; start SweepExpired in Server.Start.
5. In internal/dashboard/index.html add one `api(method, url, body)` wrapper that loads /auth/me once, adds X-Warden-CSRF on non-GET calls and sends a 401 to /auth/login?next=; replace the direct fetch() calls with it. When /auth/me is 404 (none mode) it sends no header.
6. Add internal/controlplane/session_test.go (new) with a fake clock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a session and a fake clock, when 1h01m pass idle the next request has no Principal, and with steady activity a request after 12h01m has none: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionExpiry`
- [ ] Given a valid session, when POST /dashboard/api/policy is sent with no X-Warden-CSRF, a wrong value, or a foreign Origin, then each gets 403 and the policy file is unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionCSRF`
- [ ] Given redirectURL https://cp.example/auth/callback, when a session is created, then Set-Cookie is `__Host-warden_console` with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax even though the test server is plain HTTP
- [ ] Given a logged-in user, when POST /auth/logout is sent with CSRF and the old cookie is reused on GET /auth/me, then the response is 401
- [ ] Given 10 requests within one minute, then last_seen_at is written once; and the sessions table holds the sha256 hash, never the raw id
- [ ] Given a request to /policy carrying a session cookie, when it is served, then the session store is not queried (counted with a fake store)

### 5/8 · W-P1-SSO-05

**Enforce role checks on every dashboard route**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#35](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/35)

Add the authz table and middleware that make oidc mode real: every {method, path} the dashboard serves gets a minimum role and an action name, and anything not listed is denied. The dashboard registers routes by path and switches on method inside each handler, and http.ServeMux cannot list its patterns, so this ticket exports a static route list for the table and its coverage test. Settings writes are checked per field, because SettingsWire carries llmProviders, the secrets selector and other fields that control where workers send real credentials. This ticket also removes the temporary oidc startup guard from W-P1-SSO-02.

**Requirements**

- `dashboard.Routes() []Route{Method, Path, Action string}` lists every method each handler accepts; Server.Handler() registers from the same list, so the worker dashboard (internal/worker/worker.go:581) behaves exactly as before.
- internal/controlplane/authz.go (new) table. Viewer: GET on every dashboard path, POST query, POST audit/verify. Editor: POST query/generate (it spends LLM tokens; 10 per minute per session, then 429), POST/PUT policy, POST/PUT detection, POST/PUT settings (editor fields only). Admin: POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore.
- The role is recomputed on each request with console.RoleFor(principal.Groups) against the current config. No principal: 401 JSON for /dashboard/api/*, 302 to /auth/login?next= for HTML. Too low: 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"<role>"}`. A {method, path} not in the table: 403 for every method.
- Settings: editor may change only advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents and cacheTTLSeconds. Any other difference from the live SettingsWire, including fields added later, needs admin, and the 403 body lists the fields. SetSettingsWriter changes to `func(context.Context, config.SettingsWire) error` so the CP writer can read the Principal.
- Authz wraps only the CP mount of dash.Handler(); /central/secrets is left to W-P1-SSO-06. In none mode the middleware is not installed.
- index.html reads the role from /auth/me, hides controls marked data-min-role above it, and shows the user's email and a logout button. The server stays the only enforcement point.
- Each denial logs `msg=console_authz_denied action role sub method path`; the action name is exposed on the request context for W-P1-AAUD-02.

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go add Route and Routes() (new) and make Handler() register from it; keep handler bodies unchanged.
2. Change SetSettingsWriter in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go to pass r.Context(), and update internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go and the CP call site.
3. Create internal/controlplane/authz.go (new): the table, requireRole middleware, the per-session token bucket for query/generate, and settingsFieldsChanged(live, in config.SettingsWire) []string (new).
4. In the CP settings writer passed to dash.SetSettingsWriter (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go), return a typed role error when an editor changes an admin field; map it to 403 in the dashboard settings handler.
5. In Server.Handler wrap `mux.Handle("/dashboard/", ...)` with withSession then requireRole in oidc mode, and delete the temporary oidc guard from cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
6. Update internal/dashboard/index.html for role-based hiding, and add the role matrix to docs/control-plane.md.
7. Add internal/controlplane/authz_test.go (new) with viewer, editor and admin sessions created through SessionStore.Create.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] For every Routes() entry and every role, the status matches the table (403 versus not 403): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzMatrix`
- [ ] Given a Routes() entry with no table row, when the coverage test runs, then it fails naming the route, and a request to an unlisted path gets 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage`
- [ ] Given an editor, when POST /dashboard/api/settings changes llmProviders[0].baseURL or the secrets backend, then 403 lists the field; when it changes only dlp, then 2xx
- [ ] Given a viewer, when POST /dashboard/api/secretstore or POST /dashboard/api/policy is sent, then 403; given no session, /dashboard/api/traffic gets 401 and /dashboard/ gets 302
- [ ] Given console.roles moves group eng from editor to viewer and the CP restarts, when an existing eng session POSTs /dashboard/api/policy, then 403
- [ ] Worker dashboard tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/worker`
- [ ] Given a viewer, POST /dashboard/api/query/generate gets 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"editor"}`; given an editor, the 11th call within one minute gets 429: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzQueryGenerateEditor`

### 6/8 · W-P1-SSO-06

**Require an admin session on /central/secrets and flag open consoles**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#36](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/36)

The dashboard never accepted the shared token, so W-P1-SSO-05's session requirement already keeps it off /dashboard/*. The remaining human route is `/central/secrets`, which today is gated by bearerOK (internal/controlplane/secrets.go). In oidc mode this ticket makes it require an admin session plus CSRF and ignore the bearer, and it makes none mode visible with a warning, an `authMode` field, a UI banner and an opt-in `--require-console-auth` flag.

**Requirements**

- In oidc mode handleSecrets and handleSecretByKey require an admin Principal plus CSRF; a request with only `Authorization: Bearer <cfg.Token>` gets 401 and an editor gets 403. In none mode bearerOK behaves exactly as today.
- bearerOK keeps gating /policy and /control/heartbeat, and analytics.NewIngestHandler keeps gating /central/ingest, unchanged in both modes until W-P1-WTOK-02.
- In oidc mode an Authorization header on /dashboard/* is ignored for authentication; only the session counts.
- None mode logs one startup warning ("console.auth=none: dashboard and secret writes are unauthenticated"); setupResponse (internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go) gains `authMode` (none|oidc), and index.html shows a persistent banner when it is none.
- New flag `--require-console-auth` (default false) makes the control plane refuse to start when console.auth is none.
- docs/control-plane.md replaces the note that policy editing is unauthenticated, adds a none-to-oidc migration guide, and states that scripts calling /central/secrets with the shared bearer stop working in oidc mode; secret writes then go through the admin secretstore tab until scoped API keys exist.

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/controlplane/secrets.go add secretsAuthOK(r) (new): oidc mode checks PrincipalFrom(r.Context()) for admin, else falls back to bearerOK; use it in handleSecrets and handleSecretByKey.
2. Wrap /central/secrets and /central/secrets/ in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) with withSession in oidc mode; leave /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest as they are.
3. In internal/dashboard add SetAuthMode(string) (new) and the authMode field on setupResponse; the CP sets it from Config.Console.Auth.
4. In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go add the --require-console-auth flag and the none-mode warning.
5. Update internal/dashboard/index.html for the banner and docs/control-plane.md as above.
6. Add tests in internal/controlplane/secrets_test.go, internal/dashboard and cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given oidc mode, when GET or POST /central/secrets is sent with only the shared bearer, then 401; with an admin session and CSRF, 2xx; with an editor session, 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSecretsOIDCMode`
- [ ] Given oidc mode, when GET /dashboard/api/traffic is sent with only the shared bearer, then 401
- [ ] Given either mode, when a worker uses the shared bearer on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, then responses match current behaviour: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSharedTokenWorkerRoutes`
- [ ] Given none mode, when the CP starts, then the warning is logged exactly once and GET /dashboard/api/setup returns authMode "none"; with --require-console-auth it exits non-zero
- [ ] Given none mode, existing tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy`

### 7/8 · W-P1-SSO-07

**Add Dex-backed console SSO scenario on test/harness**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#230](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/230)

Every other ticket in this feature tests against an httptest fake IdP. This test proves the done-when sentence against the real reference stack: Dex with the seeded LDAP users from W-P1-DEX-02 and a CP in oidc mode. It is a scenario on `test/harness` (marked L2 so #351 runs it on the compose stack) rather than a new rig in test/integration, and skips unless `WARDEN_IT_DEX=1`.

**Requirements**

- Lives in test/scenarios (console_sso.go, registered in scenarios_list.go with L2 true), building on `test/harness`, using the identity compose stack from W-P1-DEX-02 and the `warden-console` Dex client from W-P1-DEX-01. It skips unless `WARDEN_IT_DEX=1`, so the CI integration job from W-P1-VRFY-05 does not need Dex.
- Logs in seeded warden-viewers, warden-editors and warden-admins users through /auth/login with a cookie-jar HTTP client that submits Dex's LDAP login form; no browser is needed.
- Asserts the role matrix: viewer GET 200 and POST /dashboard/api/policy 403; editor PUT policy 2xx and settings with llmProviders 403; only admin POST /dashboard/api/integrations and POST /dashboard/api/secretstore succeed.
- Asserts that Bearer WARDEN_CP_TOKEN gets 401 on /dashboard/api/* and /central/secrets while a worker still pulls /policy.
- Asserts that an admin revoking a viewer session makes that session's next request 401.
- Test output never prints passwords, cookies, codes or tokens.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create the console SSO scenario in test/scenarios, reusing the harness API instead of test/integration helpers.
2. Start the CP with TLS on localhost:7070 (certs from scripts/gen-certs.sh, test client trusting the proxy CA) and a --config containing console.auth=oidc, issuer http://dex:5556/dex (resolved through the `127.0.0.1 dex` hosts entry from W-P1-DEX-02), clientID warden-console, redirectURL https://localhost:7070/auth/callback to match the W-P1-DEX-01 client, allowInsecureIssuer: true, the three role groups and a --state-dir in a temp dir.
3. Add a login helper (new) that follows /auth/login, posts the Dex LDAP form and returns the session cookie and CSRF token from /auth/me.
4. Run the role matrix, shared-token checks and session revocation checks as subtests.
5. Document the run command in docs/control-plane.md next to the role matrix.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With the identity compose stack running, the suite passes: `WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 go test ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/console_sso'`
- [ ] Given the warden-viewers user, POST /dashboard/api/policy returns 403 and GET /dashboard/api/traffic returns 200
- [ ] Given the shared bearer only, /dashboard/api/settings and /central/secrets return 401 while /policy returns 200
- [ ] Without WARDEN_IT_DEX=1, `go test ./test/scenarios` skips this scenario

### 8/8 · W-P1-SSO-08

**Add admin session list and revoke API**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#231](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/231)

The role is recomputed from groups stored at login, so a user removed from an IdP group keeps access until the session ends. This ticket lets an admin list live console sessions and revoke one session or every session for a user, so offboarding does not wait for the 12h absolute expiry. It uses the SessionStore.List, Delete and DeleteBySub methods from W-P1-SSO-04 and the authz table from W-P1-SSO-05.

**Requirements**

- GET /dashboard/api/sessions returns `[{handle, iss, sub, email, authMethod, createdAt, lastSeenAt, expiresAt}]`, where handle is the hex id_hash; the raw id and CSRF token are never returned.
- DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?handle=<hex> revokes one session; DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?sub=<sub> revokes every session for that subject. Unknown handles return 404.
- Both are admin in the authz table and are mounted on the CP mux only in oidc mode; the coverage test includes CP-added dashboard routes.
- Revocation takes effect on the next request (any in-memory lookup cache is cleared on delete).
- Each revoke logs `msg=console_session_revoked by_sub target_sub count`, never handles in full or cookie values.
- The dashboard gains a Sessions panel for admins listing sessions with a revoke button, using the api() wrapper.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/controlplane/sessions_admin.go (new) with handleSessionsList and handleSessionsRevoke over SessionStore.
2. Mount /dashboard/api/sessions on the CP mux ahead of /dashboard/ in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) in oidc mode, and add it as admin to the table in internal/controlplane/authz.go.
3. Extend the coverage test in internal/controlplane/authz_test.go to include CP-mounted dashboard routes.
4. Add the Sessions panel to internal/dashboard/index.html, shown only when the role is admin.
5. Add internal/controlplane/sessions_admin_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given two sessions for sub A and one for sub B, when an admin sends DELETE ?sub=A, then both A cookies get 401 on the next request and B still works: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionsRevoke`
- [ ] Given an editor, when GET or DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions is sent, then 403
- [ ] The list response contains no raw session id and no csrf field
- [ ] Given none mode, GET /dashboard/api/sessions returns 404
